text: This is the commandment—the statutes and ordinances—that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, so that you may follow them in the land you are crossing over to possess,

so that you may fear the LORD your God by keeping all his statutes and commandments that I am commanding you—you, your children, and your children's children—all the days of your life, and so that your days may be long.

versions.text: so that you may fear the LORD your God by keeping all his statutes and commandments that I am giving you—you, your children, and your children's children—all the days of your life, and so that your days may be long.
versions.explanation: The verb מְצַוֶּךָ is "command," and the chapter consistently renders this root as "command" (vv. 1, 6, 20, 24, 25). "Giving" weakens the force of the covenant charge and breaks the verbal thread.

text: Hear then, Israel, and be careful to obey, so that it may go well with you and you may increase greatly in a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, promised you.
Hear, Israel: The LORD is our God, the LORD alone.
Love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.
These words that I command you today shall be on your heart.
Impress them on your children. Speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Bind them as a sign on your hand, and let them be as bands on your forehead.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
When the LORD your God brings you into the land he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, that he would give you—great and fine cities you did not build,

versions.text: When the LORD your God brings you into the land he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, that he would give you—great and beautiful cities you did not build,
versions.explanation: טֹבֹת means "good/fine," pointing to prosperity and quality rather than aesthetic beauty. "Fine" is more accurate and reads just as smoothly aloud.

text: houses full of every good thing you did not provide, hewn cisterns you did not carve out, vineyards and olive groves you did not plant—and when you eat and are satisfied,

versions.text: houses filled with every good thing you did not fill them with, cisterns you did not dig, vineyards and olive groves you did not plant—and when you eat and are satisfied,
versions.explanation: "Filled with... you did not fill them with" is a clumsy stranded preposition that stumbles when read aloud; the smoother wording keeps the sense of receiving what one did not supply.

versions.text: houses full of every good thing you did not provide, cisterns you did not dig, vineyards and olive groves you did not plant—and when you eat and are satisfied,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has the participle חֲצוּבִים ("hewn") alongside the verb חָצַבְתָּ, a deliberate repetition: cisterns already cut from rock that the hearer did not cut. "Cisterns you did not dig" drops the participle and loses the echo; the wordplay is part of the rhetorical rhythm of the list. "Hewn cisterns you did not carve out" restores both elements and still reads cleanly aloud.

text: be careful not to forget the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Fear the LORD your God, serve him only, and take your oaths in his name.
Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you,
for the LORD your God, who is among you, is a jealous God. His anger would blaze against you, and he would wipe you from the face of the earth.
Do not put the LORD your God to the test as you tested him at Massah.
Be sure to keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and the decrees and statutes he has commanded you.

versions.text: Be sure to keep the commandments of the LORD your God, and the decrees and statutes he has given you.
versions.explanation: צִוָּךְ means "commanded you"; "given" loses the imperative force that matches the emphatic doubled verb at the start of the verse.

text: Do what is right and good in the eyes of the LORD, so that it may go well with you and you may enter and take possession of the good land the LORD promised on oath to your fathers,
driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said.
In days to come, when your child asks you, "What is the meaning of the decrees and statutes and ordinances that the LORD our God commanded you?"
tell your child: "We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
Before our very eyes the LORD sent signs and wonders, great and terrible, against Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his household.
But he brought us out from there to lead us in and give us the land he had promised on oath to our fathers.
The LORD commanded us to follow all these statutes and to fear the LORD our God, for our lasting good and to keep us alive, as is the case today.
And it will be righteousness for us if we are careful to keep this whole commandment before the LORD our God, as he has commanded us."
